lessons.title: Waves, coastal erosion and deposition

objectives: Describe how waves erode and deposit
Explain the formation of cliffs, caves, arches and stacks
Describe beaches, spits and mangrove coasts
Name ways of protecting a coast
reviewNotes: Teacher to verify the sequence and terms (hydraulic action, abrasion, attrition, solution) against the syllabus and the use of Cameroonian coastal examples.

blocks.md: Waves are made by wind blowing over the sea. Where waves reach the coast they can **erode** (wear away) or **deposit** (lay down) material. **Destructive waves** are high and steep and pull material away from the beach; **constructive waves** are low and gentle and build up the beach. Waves erode by **hydraulic action** (the force of water in cracks), **abrasion** (rocks thrown against the cliff), **attrition** (pebbles wearing each other smaller) and **solution** (dissolving).

blocks.caption: From a crack to a stack
blocks.alt: Four boxes showing the stages from a crack to a cave, an arch and a stack.

blocks.title: From cliff to stack
blocks.md: Waves attack a headland of hard rock along a crack and enlarge it into a **cave**. When two caves meet, an **arch** forms. When the roof falls, a column of rock stands apart: a **stack**. Later the stack wears down to a **stump**. At the foot of a cliff, the wearing back leaves a flat **wave-cut platform**.

blocks.title: Deposition
blocks.md: Where waves lose energy, sand and shingle are deposited to form **beaches**. A **spit** is a long ridge of sand joined to the land at one end and sticking out into the sea. A **sand bar** closes a bay. In muddy tropical estuaries, **mangrove** trees with stilt roots trap mud and protect the shore; the Cameroon coast near Douala, Limbe and Kribi has beaches, cliffs, estuaries and mangroves.

**Coastal protection** is needed where the sea eats away land or threatens towns. Methods: **sea walls** that reflect waves, **groynes** (low walls across the beach to hold sand), **rock armour** (big boulders at the cliff foot), **beach feeding** with new sand, and planting **mangroves**. People also build away from the edge and avoid removing mangroves for firewood.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Erosion wears material away; deposition lays it down. Do not use them as if they were the same.
- A stack stands in the sea, away from the headland; an arch is still joined to land on both sides.
- Groynes run across the beach; sea walls run along the shore.

blocks.title: Example 1: order of features
blocks.statement: Put these in order of formation: stack, cave, arch, crack.
steps: The sea first widens a crack in the cliff.
The crack becomes a cave; two caves meet to form an arch.
When the arch roof collapses, a stack remains.

blocks.title: Example 2: protecting a beach
blocks.statement: A beach is losing sand because the waves carry it along the shore. Suggest one method of protection and explain it.
steps: Sand moves along the coast in the direction of the waves.
Groynes built across the beach stop the sand moving.
So groynes hold sand and protect the beach.
